Tessa / Neha —

Thanks — I pulled together a draft response and attached the current subprocessor export. Key points below are what I put in the questionnaire; I also updated the PDF with per-subprocessor data-sharing boundaries.

Inline summary for Avalon’s immediate questions:
- SOC 2: We have an SOC 2 Type II in place; the most recent report covers 2025-10-01 through 2026-04-30. Auditor: ClearSky Audit Partners. Complete report available under NDA; summary attached (SOC2-summary-2026-06.pdf).
- Encryption & KMS: Customer data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. By default keys are managed in Redwood KMS (HSM-backed). For Avalon PHI usage we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS with a dedicated key policy — we’ll include KMS instructions if they want CMK.
- Subprocessors: see redwood_subprocessors_v2.pdf attached. Short list relevant to PHI: (1) Redwood Serving (hosted model inference) — managed by Redwood, runs in customer-isolated VPC for Dedicated/Private; (2) Cloud provider compute (AWS/GCP) — raw compute only; (3) Logging/Telemetry (Datadog/LogDNA) — telemetry is pseudonymized by default and PHI is not sent to third-party telemetry unless explicitly enabled by customer; (4) Storage (S3/GCS) for model artifacts and optional persistent caches — access controlled and audit logged.
- BAA: We can provide a standard BAA; Neha, can you drop the template here and I’ll confirm any technical addendums needed for specific subprocessors/CMK?

Open items for the questionnaire I could not fully answer inline:
- Specific retention windows for telemetry when enabled (product to confirm default and configurable values).
- If Avalon wants CMK, ops will need a short onboarding checklist to configure VPC peering and KMS grants.

I attached: redwood_subprocessors_v2.pdf (with data boundary columns) and a completed draft of Avalon_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (answers in-sheet). Let me know if you want me to redact anything before sending to Avalon.
